summary:
Centro contains two of Italy's six highest-victim regions for anti-LGBT violence (Lazio, Toscana per the Progetto Gionata 2012-2025 region-by-region study) and saw an activist assaulted at the Piceno Pride march in Ascoli Piceno (June 2025) with his flag seized and destroyed. Rome Pride was also targeted politically in the same June 2025 wave (the Naples Pride was attacked in the same wave but sits in Sud). The unit also contains the strongest positive institutional response found anywhere in Italy: a January 2025 Bologna first-instance conviction that recognised a "transphobic motive" behind a punitive rape of a trans sex worker, awarded damages, and - for the first time - admitted the Movimento Identita Trans as civil party. This is a judicial signal that transphobic violence is prosecuted as a distinct aggravating factor, and it applies to visitors who would rely on the same courts.

Net deviation: +0.02 above the national score (0.50). The high-victim data for Lazio and Toscana are concerning but are offset by the Bologna precedent and the absence of any criminalisation, facility ban, or enforcement mechanism targeting a visitor. The Ascoli Piceno incident is a single event with no patterned institutional failure. Compared to Nord-Ovest (0.47), Centro trades lower violence-concentration (no Alessandria killing or Brianza Roman-salute episode) for a stronger judicial response; compared to Sud (0.44), Centro lacks the railway-station public-exposure incidents and the ILGA-Europe "geographic spread" finding.

sources.summary: Dire news-agency report (24 Jan 2025): a Bologna first-instance court recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the trans-movement association that helps sex workers, and for the first time admitted the Movimento Identita Trans (MIT) as civil party - the strongest judicial recognition of transphobic aggravation recorded in this country.

Progetto Gionata region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the Italian regions with the highest victim counts, six of them ranking at the top; Lazio and Toscana (both inside Centro) are two of the six highest-victim regions, alongside Lombardia, Piemonte (Nord-Ovest), Campania and Puglia (Sud). Provides the per-region violence distribution used to score all Italian units.

Corriere Adriatico report (June 2025): activist Raniero Bertone was assaulted during the Piceno Pride march in Ascoli Piceno between the public gardens and Piazza Arringo; his rainbow flag bearing a six-pointed star was seized and thrown away - the only recorded physical attack on a Pride participant inside Centro, a single event with no institutional follow-up failure documented.

tangentialFactors: Rome Pride was targeted politically over the Middle East conflict (June 2025 wave) - a protest-visibility climate affecting LGBT events generally rather than a trans-specific legal mechanism.
localsOnly: The Rebibbia specialized prison section and the male-prison placement policy (Rome, Lazio) concern resident detainees; they do not change a visitor's exposure beyond the national prison framework.
